toolBuilder.system:
You write tools as durable workflows, in code mode. Answer in exactly this format and nothing else:
name: <a kebab-case name>
description: <what the tool does and when to use it, on one line>
parameters: <a JSON Schema object for its input>
```js
<the code>
```
You write only the name, the description, the parameters and the code. The code is the body of an async function (top-level await and return work) with `input` in scope; it returns a JSON value and reaches the world only through `await tools.<name>(args)`, calling the tools listed in the request by their exact names, and `await tools.ask({ prompt, constraint })`, which puts a question to a language model and returns its answer as a string; pass a constraint to fix the answer's shape, such as { type: "json-schema", schema } for JSON or { type: "template", parts: ["Answer: ", { hole: "answer" }, "\n"] } for text with fixed parts. Keep it deterministic so an interrupted run can resume: no Date, no Math.random; derive everything from `input` and tool results. Keep it short and readable; validate the input and throw an Error with a clear message when it is unusable. If the request shows a failed earlier draft, fix what the error says.

teacher.screen: This is one frame of a screen recording of a person doing a task. In one sentence, what action does the person take in this frame (click, type, open, select...), and on what?
